finding: Arrangements for banks to lend one million dollars if required by Legislature; recommends consummating agreement and another million on bonds.
limit: Financing arrangement and recommendation, not cash received or inability to maintain a particular camp. Wrong actor/state for C03.

finding: Board recommends liberal support to volunteer corps bearing heavy expenses; urges a regular paid garrison and military bureau. Some expenditure occurred under Governor advice; full accounts not rendered.
limit: Own signature as Board president establishes knowledge by February14; no inference that all volunteers stayed home or camp fund was exhausted.

finding: Schedule totals $32670.91; includes January14 $257 board/quarters for troops, January17 $2500 commissary expense, January30 $750 debts/supplies for February.
limit: Warrants drawn are not cash balances or remaining appropriation. Heading says December12 1861 [sic]; no silent correction or money-to-men conversion.

finding: Regular-force organisation proceeding slowly under three-year term; four-month troops retained for forts; expects Confederate protection when their terms expire.
limit: Not evidence of April camp-finance shortage; different forces and undertakings.

finding: Asks New Orleans muster and allocation of transportation cost; sends act authorising regular-force transfer and permission for volunteers to tender Confederate service.
limit: Expense expectation after Confederate receipt is not an independent camp-finance balance. Own approval dates knowledge of act.

finding: Apart from a small number of volunteer companies Harris reports no military organisation; militia disorganised after repeal of drill/parade requirement; asks reorganisation.
limit: Self-authored statement, not a later reply. State as of January7 only; no automatic persistence to April22 or model July3; no invented receipt delay.

finding: Sections187-189: Governor commander-in-chief except forces in United States service; appoints adjutant-general/staff; custody of public arms.
limit: Publication date only year1858; exact receipt by Harris not established. Office alone is not proof of unrestricted extra-state levy/transfer authority.

finding: Sections469-476 preserve older militia laws except conflicting code provisions; repeal scheduled drills; prescribe assessor and county-clerk reports.
limit: Older laws expressly survive. These pages cannot prove absence of every power to order troops outside Tennessee. Jan7 message supplies personal knowledge of disorganisation, not a legal exhaustion proof.

finding: Disclaims authority to order beyond State and says organisation defective while undertaking three regiments.
limit: Measured answer; excluded as source of its own conditions.

finding: Says State lacks means to keep men instantly available in camp and asks immediate Confederate muster.
limit: Measured answer; excluded as source of its own conditions.

finding: Requests immediate volunteer organisation, maintenance appropriations and military board.
limit: After cutoff; cannot backdate even where text mentions January.
